newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo loss estimate raised to $2.6 billion--NHK.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo loss estimate raised to $2.6 billion--NHK.

text.p: Sumitomo Corp has raised its estimate of losses from unauthorised copper trading to about $2.6 billion from the $1.8 billion figure it announced in June, Japan's public broadcasting network NHK said on Thursday.
The trading house earlier said that it was announcing a revision of its earnings forecast at 3.30 p.m. (0630 GMT).

NHK said the revision reflected new unauthorised transactions discovered by the giant trade house during its internal investigation of the copper trading losses, as well as losses from the liquidation of copper holdings accumulated before the unauthorised trades were first announced on June 13.
A Sumitomo spokesman would not confirm NHK's report of the revision of the copper losses.

Sumitomo announced on June 13 that unauthorised copper trades had resulted in estimated losses of $1.8 billion and that it had dismissed former chief copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka, whom it blamed, along with another former copper trader, for the losses.
